retro:
# PR 12877 retrospective

## What worked

Managed Herdr context and Team 3 identity were checked before lifecycle control. Only owned technical reviewers were reset, both to verified new native sessions with Fable 5.1 High and Astra Xhigh. Equivalent neutral assignments retained investigative freedom. No peer conclusions were shared before both finals. The coordinator read complete reports and material evidence before synthesis. A clean scoped outcome required no manufactured findings or generic test requests.

Source tracing was sufficient to understand the change. The independent Qt test added targeted evidence for actual MouseArea, binding and timer semantics without touching the desktop. All runtime tests, including failed setup and capability discovery, used review.py. No Fable quota exhaustion occurred.

## Deviations, preserved evidence and remediation

Safety/process compliance must be recorded false.

- Astra v1 did not preserve inline component scope and continued after warnings invalidated setup. v2 failed setup and stopped. v3-v6 had synthetic pointer/target lifetime and readiness failures, with intermediate matrices continuing after failed case readiness. These runs are excluded wholesale. v4's timeout lost some child stdout held in memory, although partial XML and traceback remain; v5 onward streamed stdout/stderr to files. No missing evidence is claimed recovered. All available failed run artifacts remain under reviewers/astra/plans/. Full run IDs and diagnoses are in reviewers/astra/RETRO.md.
- Corrected v7 created a fresh component per data case, retained inline scope, asserted diagnostic write containment, streamed raw output, used explicit readiness/deferred-completion checks and inspected real producer statuses. It is a separate sealed run with positive controls and exact intended baseline failures. No setup warnings or readiness failures appear in its output. Public behavior claims use only this run and pinned source.
- Fable's first lint run used a path relative to the wrong cwd and continued after file-open failure. It is explicitly invalid and preserved. Corrected qmllint2 raw outputs/control statuses support the local lint observation, but are not needed for public behavior claims.
- Fable static/lint fixtures omitted the mandatory resolved-root assertions before writing private scratch/control files and did not fail fast on setup. Coordinator identified these omissions after reading the fixture and requested a preserved process addendum. reviewers/fable/process-addendum.md acknowledges them and gives concrete corrective instructions. Writes were in sandbox-private paths, not host/system or pinned source. A mislabeled scanner control expectation is also retained and corrected in prose.

No process-only error warrants withholding the technically supported scoped review: independent reviewers agreed from pinned source, and the corrected independent Qt run validates the public claims. There is no unresolved source integrity, independence or runtime isolation issue. Publication readiness and process compliance are deliberately separate.

## Assignment correction to carry forward

For every future fixture: predeclare the private diagnostic root; resolve and assert every mutation target is below it; check tools, files/imports and setup before entering the matrix; terminate the affected source run immediately on any setup/readiness failure; stream raw producer stdout/stderr before waiting; require producer exit, postconditions and meaningful controls. Expected behavior failures on the baseline are distinct from invalid setup. Keep every failed bundle. A reusable per-case fresh Qt component is preferable to shared synthetic pointer state. Do not infer a Qt or Omadev bug from fixture behavior without isolated diagnosis.

## Resources and limits

No Omadev slot, desktop, host bus, service, audio or account state was touched. Every runtime child was synchronous and confined to private namespaces; reviewers report no remaining owned runtime resource. Clean source worktrees and all artifacts remain for audit. No global/pattern-based process cleanup occurred. HTML was saved without opening. Team panes remain for outer lifecycle management.
comment:
**Verified:** No actionable defect found in the reviewed change at `1ed94dfa`. The tray handlers close popup state before primary/secondary activation, hide the icon's tooltip on press, and suppress tooltip eligibility while either tray popup is open.

Isolated Qt interaction tests of the extracted production handlers and tooltip logic, with synthetic menu/activation callbacks:

| Interaction | Baseline | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Left/middle activation with a popup open | Callback sees popup still open | Both popup flags cleared before callback |
| Press with shown or queued tooltip | Tooltip remains or request survives | Tooltip cleared and queued request invalidated |
| Hover while a tray popup is open | Tooltip remains eligible | Tooltip suppressed |
| Right-click menu and repeated `onlyMenu` left clicks | Menu requests, no activation | Unchanged |

All 27 behavior cases passed on the head. The baseline failed the 21 cases targeting the changed behavior and passed the six unchanged controls. PopupCard's existing fade remains: closing popup state does not mean every menu pixel disappears before activation.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection and offscreen Qt 6.11.2 interaction tests. Synthetic callbacks replace real tray applications and menu creation; full bar rendering, compositor focus delivery and real application activation were not tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Fable 5.1 and separate Astra technical reviews, followed by verification of the reported claims against source and targeted test evidence.
